title: Arnold trained like an idiot？
summary: NH defends Arnold's lifting technique against influencer critics, including rounded-back cable and T-bar rows, his lat pulldowns, bent-arm flyes and power raises. He then criticises the Blueprint to Mass program as far too much volume for naturals and calls its shock-the-muscle intensity techniques junk. Instead he recommends rest-pause, extending drop sets, back-off sets and keeping the same exercises over time.
claims: Much of the online criticism of Arnold's form comes from people who do not understand that proper bodybuilding form is not pretty form
A cable row done with a rigidly straight back and fixed shoulders turns into a biceps isolation exercise because only the arms move
Letting the shoulders protract and the upper back round on cable rows makes the back musculature the main mover, as Arnold did
For back training, scapular protraction to stretch the back matters more than retraction; holding retraction throughout keeps the back from being challenged
The popular cue to keep the shoulders back on rows and lat work is the opposite of what you should cue, and explains why many men cannot feel their lats
Arnold's spinal flexion on rows was somewhat exaggerated; NH would not go into that deep a stretch
A row becomes a cheat when the movement comes from the hips in a pendulum motion, using torso weight to move the stack, like a rower in a boat
Rounded-back T-bar rows are not really dangerous as long as the posterior chain is engaged and loads are moderate; they fatigue the erectors and load the lower back, so account for that
A rounded-back deadlift to move maximal weight is detrimental, unlike a rounded row with lighter load
Program the deficit T-bar row as a total-back exercise; it is tough without the mobility, so work up to it
Do not copy Arnold's touch-and-go on T-bar rows; bouncing off the floor steals part of the stretch and leaves growth on the table
Leaning back and bringing the bar to the chest on pulldowns is valid and allows more weight, but NH prefers a vertical pull and slower tempo
On pulldowns, let the scapula move freely and let the stack stretch the lats at the top; stop the stretch if the shoulders take over and internally rotate

Cueing people with poor mobility to bring the bar to the chest makes them internally rotate and flare the elbows; instead think of squeezing the scapulae and accept a shorter range until strength and mobility build

Arnold seemed to stop pulldown sets around 3 RIR; that worked with his high volume, but on 3-6 sets per muscle or exercise per day every set should go close to failure, and pulldowns can safely be taken to failure plus negatives
Heavy flyes cannot widen the chest; pec shape comes from tendon insertions, and NH has high insertions giving a round chest
Flyes still help build the lower pecs, feel good and help thoracic mobility
Keep the elbow bent at about 90 degrees on flyes; straightening the arm creates a weak link, lowers the load and raises overuse injury risk without more chest work
Power raises are as close to pure side-delt isolation as possible, with peak tension at the bottom stretch, unlike cable laterals where the arm hits the body and tension dies
Power raises can be dangerous so build up to them; they allow safe cheating and lengthened partials at the end of the set
The Blueprint to Mass is not a bro split but an upper/lower-style split trained 6 days a week, with abs, calves and forearms included
Rotating exercises week to week to shock the muscle lowers specificity
Rep schemes like 8 down to 2 make no sense; with an 8RM a second set gives 6-7 reps and a third about 5, never 2
Blueprint to Mass has far too much upper-body volume for a natural: 4 back exercises in a day and shoulder supersets of overlapping exercises for small muscles with low work capacity
For naturals, 1-2 shoulder isolation movements on a given day plus one or two vertical presses is enough
The program's leg days are the best: squat, stiff-leg deadlift, lunges, leg extensions; one big quad move, one posterior-chain move, 1-2 isolations
Instead of daily 4x25 abs with no progression, do 3 sets of 8-12 with real progressive overload
You could cut 30-40% of the program's volume and get similar results
People who run Blueprint to Mass often quit after eight weeks; a good program should be sustainable for months
As a natural the rule is to do as little as possible to get as much as possible because recovery is lower; extra volume is junk volume
Arnold's 1-to-10 method, a 1RM then descending to 10 reps without rest, is bad for hypertrophy and raises injury risk; a 6x10 would be better and it is fine only once every six months for fun
The stripping method, dropping weight to the bar for 20 reps without rest, produces junk volume driven by fatigue
Pyramiding 25-20-15-10-8-5-3 to a 1RM ends with a pointless max at near-maximal fatigue; a 1RM is pointless for hypertrophy
Muscle does not need to be confused; its function is to move a lever and get stronger when challenged
Intensity techniques must be added on top of a quality set, never replace it
Rest-pause is his favorite technique: go to failure, rest 30 seconds, get more reps; use it on Smith presses and cable and biceps isolations
Rest-pause breaks plateaus: if stuck at 10 reps on lateral raises aiming for 15, do 10, rest 30 seconds and get 5 more, then increase the weight
Use drop sets only to extend a set to its target reps once rest-pause fails, e.g. dropping 5-10 lb on cable triceps extensions after hitting failure at 10 of 15
Use a back-off set when you can no longer hit the rep range with the top weight; reduce slightly and still go close to failure
Rotating bench angles every week hurts specificity and can make you regress; keep low and high incline variations both in the program and alternate them
Pick one movement; when it stalls add a variation; two variations can give a year of gains before adding a third
Fast progress on a new exercise is adaptation, not growth; growth happens when you start struggling for reps, so swapping exercises whenever they slow down keeps muscles small
Soreness from a new exercise shows lack of adaptation, not progress; long-term soreness from a lift like RDLs can be a sign it works
Arnold's training philosophy is the real problem; ideas like shocking the muscle may have been said to sound cool on camera
Think for yourself; do not blindly follow charismatic idols or the people who attack them for clickbait
exercises: let the shoulders protract and the upper back round; no pendulum from the hips
back becomes the prime mover instead of the biceps
rounded back allowed with posterior chain engaged and moderate load; no touch-and-go
free scapula, full stretch at the top, stop before shoulders internally rotate; vertical pull with slow tempo preferred
more load, better stretch, lower overuse risk
build up gradually; cheat safely; lengthened partials
side-delt isolation with peak tension at the stretch
good but tension dies at the bottom
drop 5-10 lb at failure to finish target reps
still makes him sore after years, sign it builds the posterior chain
